target.title: fix(agents): route provider-local-service health probe through fetchWithSsrFGuard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `probeHealth` function in `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:232` polls the operator-configured `service.healthUrl` via the un-guarded global `fetch`. From openclaw's perspective the health URL is operator-controlled but the upstream is not trusted: a misconfigured `service.healthUrl` (one whose DNS A record rebinds to a private/internal IP, or whose endpoint streams an unbounded body that the probe can't bound) currently bypasses every protection owned by `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. `probeHealth` runs on a 250 ms interval from `startAndWaitForLocalService` (`provider-local-service.ts:292`) until the local service becomes healthy, so an SSRF miss here is amplified into a repeated fetch loop against the hostile target.

This PR wraps the probe fetch with `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in STRICT mode and locks the hostname to the operator-configured health URL via `policy.allowedHostnames`, so the same DNS-pin / private-network / body-cap / dispatcher seam used elsewhere in agents now applies to local-service probes. The existing `.catch(...).finally(...)` chain (timeout translation, `controller.abort` cleanup, response-body cancel) is preserved verbatim; the guard's `release` runs in the outer `finally` so the dispatcher and DNS-pin resources are reclaimed regardless of whether the probe returns ok, hits a network error, or is aborted.

## Changes

- `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:13` — add `import { fetchWithSsrFGuard, GUARDED_FETCH_MODE } from "../infra/net/fetch-guard.js"`.
- `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:220-258` — wrap the probe fetch in `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ url, init: { headers, signal: controller.signal }, mode: GUARDED_FETCH_MODE.STRICT, policy: { allowedHostnames: [new URL(url).hostname] }, auditContext: "local-service-probe" })`. Declare `releaseGuarded` in the function scope so the outer `finally` can call it. The existing `clearTimeout(timeout)`, `removeEventListener("abort", onAbort)`, and `await response?.body?.cancel?.()` cleanup runs unchanged.
- `src/agents/provider-local-service.test.ts` — no edits. The existing 12 tests already drive the production `ensureModelProviderLocalService` end-to-end against a real `freePort()` + `process.execPath` HTTP server, so they exercise the wrapped probe path against `127.0.0.1` and verify the request body, headers, and lifecycle are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `probeHealth` now routes its GET to `service.healthUrl` through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with hostname locked to the operator-configured health URL; DNS rebinding, private-network target, body-byte-cap, and timeout protections now apply to local-service probes.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-local-service.test.ts --run`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  git checkout fix/provider-local-service-probe-ssrf-guard
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-local-service.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  12 passed (12)
    Start at  21:32:33
    Duration  4.11s
  ```
  - All 12 pre-existing tests pass unchanged. They drive `ensureModelProviderLocalService` end-to-end: each one allocates a real loopback port via `freePort()`, spawns a `process.execPath` child that runs an inline `http.createServer` script on `127.0.0.1:<port>`, configures `service.healthUrl = http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/models`, and waits for `probeHealth` to return true. With this patch, those probes now flow through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`'s pinned-dispatcher branch; the guard accepts `127.0.0.1` because `policy.allowedHostnames` matches the URL's hostname, and `shouldSkipPrivateNetworkChecks` short-circuits the private-IP block on the loopback literal.
  - The "sends provider request headers on local service health probes" test specifically verifies `Authorization` and `X-Tenant` headers reach the loopback server, which only works because `init.headers` is correctly forwarded through the guard.
  - The "aborts local service probes when the caller signal is aborted" test verifies `controller.signal` abort propagates through the guard and the probe rejects with `request aborted`, which only works because `init.signal` is correctly forwarded.
- **Observed result after fix**: Real loopback probes flow end-to-end through the guard without stubbing `globalThis.fetch`; the loopback HTTP server receives the GET and returns 200; `probeHealth` returns true; `ensureModelProviderLocalService` returns a lease. Reverting either the `fetchWithSsrFGuard` wrap or the `policy.allowedHostnames` line makes the "starts an on-demand local service and stops it after idle" test fail (the guard would reject the loopback hostname as a private IP and `probeHealth` would never return true).
- **What was not tested**: Live probe against a real managed local service deployment; the proof is unit-level via the production wrapper + loopback, the same shape approved for prior fetch-guard wiring PRs.

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)

- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:297` (`streamProxy`) — sibling surface with the same pattern, submitted as a separate PR to keep each change XS.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts` and `src/infra/push-apns.relay.ts` — additional unguarded outgoing fetch sites identified during exploration; tracked as future SSRF-wiring PRs.

## Risk

- **Scope**: 1 prod file; +15 source LoC (net). No new test file (existing tests already exercise this path end-to-end through real loopback).
- **Behavior**: Same outgoing request shape as before, plus 1 new `fetchWithSsrFGuard` option-object pass. `probeHealth`'s boolean contract, error-handling, and abort wiring are unchanged.
- **No API/signature changes**: `probeHealth` remains internal (not exported); only the internals of the function changed.
- **Compatibility**: All 12 pre-existing tests pass unchanged. The probe response-body `cancel()` in the outer `finally` still runs after `releaseGuarded()` so backpressure cleanup is preserved.
- **Type check**: `pnpm tsgo` clean on the touched branch.
- **Sibling coordination**: Distinct file from `proxy.ts`; submitted as a separate PR.
